holidays.name: National Love a Tree Day
holidays.description: A day to give your leafy neighbors some credit. Hug a trunk, read under a canopy, have a picnic in the shade, or plant a sapling. Trees give us shade, snacks, oxygen, and a place to hang a hammock.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and its founder is unclear. It falls in mid-May, when trees are in fresh leaf across much of the Northern Hemisphere.
holidays.funFact: Trees are the reason you can eat a fresh fruit pie in the shade. Apples, cherries, and peaches all grow on trees.

holidays.name: National Coquilles Saint Jacques Day
holidays.description: A day for fancy scallop lovers. Coquilles Saint Jacques is a classic French dish of tender scallops in a creamy wine sauce, topped with breadcrumbs and cheese. It is then broiled until golden and bubbly. It is a good excuse to feel like a French bistro chef in your own kitchen.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates a dish from French cuisine that is traditionally served in a scallop shell.
holidays.funFact: The name means 'scallops of Saint James' in French. The scallop shell is also the traditional emblem of pilgrims on the Camino de Santiago.

holidays.name: National Biographer's Day
holidays.description: A salute to the people who write other people's life stories. It is a day to read a biography, or to write down a few chapters about someone in your own life.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of the day Samuel Johnson first met his future biographer, James Boswell, in a London bookshop on May 16, 1763. Boswell's 'Life of Samuel Johnson' later became one of the most famous biographies in English.
holidays.funFact: Boswell's biography of Johnson is so well known that 'Boswell' became a word for a devoted biographer.
